[Back to the lesson](positional-encoding.qmd) · [Learning path plan](review-path.qmd#representations)

## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- Two occurrences of the same token can start with the same embedding. Their ranks in the sequence provide information distinct from token identity.
- An additive absolute encoding can combine the token embedding with a vector for its position at the input.
- RoPE uses position to rotate Q and K after projection. Their dot product then depends on the relative offset.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

After tokenization, swap the positions of two IDs in the sequence. Do their rows in the embedding table change?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No, their IDs select the same rows. Their sequence positions change, which can affect the resulting contextual states.

</details>

::: {.visual-recall}

### Visual card — Same token, two positions {#visual-recall}

Tokenization assigned the same ID to both occurrences of `chat`. With additive absolute position encoding, which slots match across the two positions, and which may contain different vectors?

```{=html}
<div class="visual-recall__diagram" role="img" aria-label="Two rows. Position 0, token chat, slot A for the embedding, plus slot B for position. Position 3, token chat, slot C for the embedding, plus slot D for position.">
  <div class="visual-recall__lane">
    <span class="visual-recall__node"><code>chat</code> · position 0</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__operator">→</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__slot"><strong>A</strong> · embedding</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__operator">+</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__slot"><strong>B</strong> · position</span>
  </div>
  <div class="visual-recall__lane">
    <span class="visual-recall__node"><code>chat</code> · position 3</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__operator">→</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__slot"><strong>C</strong> · embedding</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__operator">+</span>
    <span class="visual-recall__slot"><strong>D</strong> · position</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

<details>
<summary>Show the card answer</summary>

**A and C** are the same embedding. The ID selects the same table row at both positions. **B and D** are the vectors for positions 0 and 3. They can differ even though the token is the same.

</details>

:::
